green tea polyphenol (GTP) treatment of human breast cancer cells inhibited constitutively active AP-1 and nuclear factor-kappaB (NF-kappaB) transcription factors, suppressed secretion of uPA from breast cancer cells, inhibited the invasive behavior of these cells, and decreased formation of cell adhesion, migration, and invasion complexes.
green tea polyphenol inhibits invasive behavior of breast carcinoma cells by down regulating transcription factors AP- and NF-κ, which results in inhibition of urokinse plasminogen activity.

green tea polyphenol treatment inhibits the invasive behavior of human breast cancer cells by suppressing the constitutive activation of AP-1 and the NF-κB signaling pathway, which further results in the inhibition of uPA secretion.

the effect of GCPs on human breast cancer cell lines.
the effect of GCP on the invasive behavior of human breast cancer cells.
the effects of green tea poly-phenols on breast cancer cells.

the green tea polyphenol treatment of breast cancer cells inhibited their invasive behavior through inhibition of the constitutively active AP-1 and/or NF-κB transcription factors, which in turn inhibited the secretion of uPA from breast cancer cells.
